sections.section_title: Clearing the tim_ocxref signal on an external event
sections.text_helper: Section 35.5.21 "Clearing the tim_ocxref signal on an external event" in chapter 35 (General purpose timers (TIM15/TIM16/TIM17)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1386.
sections.section_content:
The tim_ocxref signal of a given channel can be cleared when a high level is applied on the
tim_ocref_clr_int input (OCxCE enable bit in the corresponding TIM_CCMRx register set to
1). tim_ocxref remains low until the next transition to the active state, on the following PWM
cycle. This function can only be used in Output compare and PWM modes. It must not be
used in Forced mode.
The tim_ocref_clr_int input can be selected among several inputs, as shown on Figure515
below.
[Figure 515. tim_ocref_clr input selection multiplexer]
This feature is also supported in combined and asymmetric modes. In this case, it is
mandatory to have the OCxCE bit enabled for the channel, the OCxCE bit of the
complementary channel (for example OC2CE = X for oc2ref in Figure516) is ignored in this
case.
Figure516 to Figure518 are describing the output waveforms for some use cases, when
the ocref_clr_int signal is asserted.

Conditions of use
This feature is intended to support cycle-by-cycle current control loops, typically with a
comparator shortening the PWM on-time when a current threshold is exceeded.
It cannot be used for the following modes, where the OCxCE bit must be cleared:
• PWM toggle mode (OCxM[4:0] = 0x03)
• One pulse mode with PWM active on match (OPM=1 and OCxM[4:0] = 0x06, 0x08,
0x0C, 0x0E)
• Combined PWM mode 1 in center aligned mode (CMS[1:0] = 1,2,3 and
OCxM[4:0]=0x0C)
